Core vocabulary (5 words)

Table 48 — Grid vocabulary
WordMeaning
TrackOne row or one column
LineThe boundary between tracks (numbered: 1, 2, 3…)
CellIntersection of one row + one column
AreaNamed rectangle of cells ("header header")
frFraction of FREE space (1fr 2fr = 1/3 + 2/3)
CODE  ·  Your first grid (3 equal columns, responsive gap)
.gallery { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr; gap: 20px; }

The one-line responsive grid (no media queries!)

CODE  ·  The most famous line in modern CSS
.auto-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(260px, 1fr));
  gap: 20px;
}
Think of it like this — repeat(auto-fit, minmax(260px, 1fr)) is smart shelving

"Fit as many 260px-wide boxes as the shelf allows; stretch them to share leftover space; drop whole columns when the shelf shrinks." Desktop shows 4 across, tablet 2, phone 1 — zero breakpoints written.

Table 49 — repeat() decoded
PieceJob
repeat(n, …)Repeat a track pattern n times
auto-fitFit as many tracks as possible (collapse empty ones)
minmax(260px, 1fr)Each track: minimum 260px, maximum equal share
1frOne fraction of leftover space

Placement: lines, span, areas

CODE  ·  Method 1 — line numbers (dashboards)
.dash { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr 1fr; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr; gap: 16px; }
.widget-big { grid-column: 2 / 4; grid-row: 1 / 3; }  /* from line 2 to 4, rows 1-2 */
/* span shortcut: "take 2 columns from wherever I am" */
.widget-wide { grid-column: span 2; }
CODE  ·  Method 2 — named areas (page scaffolding, most readable)
.page {
  display: grid; min-height: 100vh;
  grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr;
  grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto;
  grid-template-areas:
    "header header"
    "side   main"
    "footer footer";
}
.site-header { grid-area: header; } .site-side { grid-area: side; }
.site-main { grid-area: main; }     .site-footer { grid-area: footer; }
@media (max-width: 720px) {
  .page { grid-template-columns: 1fr;
    grid-template-areas: "header" "main" "side" "footer"; }
}

Alignment: two axes at once

Table 50 — Grid alignment (justify = row axis, align = column axis)
ScopeRow axisColumn axis
Whole tracks in containerjustify-contentalign-content
Default for all itemsjustify-itemsalign-items
One item overridejustify-selfalign-self
CODE  ·  Center anything in a grid cell (or the whole grid)
.cell-center { display: grid; place-items: center; }  /* align + justify shorthand */
Key takeaway — Key takeaway

Layout decision tree: page scaffolding or 2D gallery → Grid (areas/lines). Row/column of components → Flexbox. Unknown-size centering → either (place-items: center vs flex centering — pick the one already in use nearby).

Quick check — grid-column: 2 / 4 means…
  1. Column 2 only
  2. From line 2 to line 4 (spans 2 tracks)
  3. 2 divided by 4
  4. Rows 2–4
Answer: B  ·  Grid placement uses LINE numbers: start line 2, end line 4 = occupies tracks 2 and 3.
Exercise 17 — Dashboard layout

Header spanning full width, sidebar 240px, 4 stat cards in responsive auto-fit grid, footer full width. Stack to one column under 720px.

Solution

Page scaffolding via areas (header/side/main/footer as above); stats inside main with .stats{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(180px,1fr));gap:16px}; media query collapsing areas to one column. Grid-inside-Grid: each level does one job.

Chapter 19

Responsive Design — Mobile First

Intermediate~ 100 min
One codebase, every screen: fluid units, media queries, responsive images and testing.
In this chapter
  • Mobile-first philosophy
  • Media query breakpoints that make sense
  • Fluid type with clamp()
  • Responsive images + videos

Gamal responsiveElzero media queriesAngela §Responsive

Mobile-first philosophy

Write CSS for the phone first, then ADD rules as screens grow (min-width). Desktops get enhancements; phones get the fast core. The opposite (desktop-first with max-width) ships desktop weight to phones — backwards.

CODE  ·  Mobile-first in action
/* Base = phone (everyone gets this) */
.cards { display: grid; gap: 16px; }
/* ≥640px: two columns */
@media (min-width: 640px) { .cards { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; } }
/* ≥1024px: sidebar layout appears */
@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  .layout { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 260px 1fr; }
}
Table 51 — Breakpoints that make sense (content-based, not device-based)
BreakpointNameTypical change
≥640pxSmall tablet2-column grids, bigger type
≥768pxTabletNav expands, side-by-side sections
≥1024pxLaptopSidebars, multi-column dashboards
≥1280pxDesktopMax-width container caps growth (Ch 14)
Warning — Never target specific devices

@media (max-width: 375px) for "iPhone X" breaks on the next phone. Instead: shrink your browser until the layout looks bad — THAT pixel value is your breakpoint. Design responds to content, not to Apple.

Fluid typography with clamp()

CODE  ·  Text that scales smoothly — no breakpoints needed
h1 { font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 1rem + 4vw, 3.5rem); }
/*       minimum   preferred (fluid)    maximum    */
/* Phone: 28px → grows with screen → caps at 56px */
body { font-size: clamp(1rem, 0.9rem + 0.5vw, 1.125rem); }
Table 52 — clamp() decoded: `clamp(MIN, FLUID, MAX)`
PartJob
MINNever smaller (readability floor)
FLUID (vw-based)Grows with the viewport
MAXNever bigger (design ceiling)

Responsive media (never overflow again)

CODE  ·  Media that behaves on every screen
img, video { max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }
.hero-video { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; }
/* Tables on phones: scroll inside, page never breaks */
.table-scroll { overflow-x: auto; }
Try it yourself — The 375px test (5 minutes)

DevTools → Toggle device toolbar (Ctrl+Shift+M) → 375×667. Scroll your whole page: no horizontal scrollbar? Tap targets ≥44px? Text readable without zoom? Tables scroll inside their box? Fix failures with fluid widths, wrapping flex, and smaller clamp() minimums.

Responsive ship checklist
  • - viewport meta present; no horizontal scroll at 360px
  • - Touch targets ≥ 44×44px; no hover-only features (phones have no hover!)
  • - Type fluid via clamp(); line length ≤ 70ch
  • - Images WebP/AVIF + lazy below fold; hero not lazy
  • - Tables wrapped in scroll containers; test 360px + 768px + 1440px
Quick check — Mobile-first means…
  1. Design phones, then enhance with min-width
  2. Design desktop, then max-width fixes
  3. Two separate sites
  4. Phones only
Answer: A  ·  Base styles = phone; min-width queries add complexity upward. One codebase, layered.
Exercise 18 — Make it responsive

Take your Ch 9 profile page (unstyled): add container, clamp() headings, auto-fit gallery, stacked→side nav at 768px, scroll-safe table. Test at 360/768/1440.

Solution

.container{width:100%;max-width:1000px;margin:auto;padding:0 16px}, h1{font-size:clamp(2rem,1.2rem+4vw,3.5rem)}, .gallery{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(220px,1fr))}, nav column→row at 768px. Verify zero horizontal scroll everywhere.

Transitions, Transforms and Animations

Intermediate~ 90 min
Motion that feels expensive: hover effects, loaders, reveals — all on the GPU fast-path.
In this chapter

transition: smooth A→B changes

CODE  ·  Every hover effect is this pattern
.btn { background: navy; transition: background 0.25s ease, transform 0.25s ease; }
.btn:hover { background: royalblue; transform: translateY(-2px); }
.card { transition: box-shadow 0.3s ease; }
.card:hover { box-shadow: 0 18px 40px rgb(2 6 23 / 0.14); }
Table 53 — transition anatomy: `background 0.25s ease 0s`
PartMeaningPro choice
propertyWhat animates (or all — lazy, avoid)List exact properties
durationHow long150–300ms UI; up to 600ms big reveals
timingSpeed curveease default; ease-out for entrances
delayWait before startingStagger effects (0.05s steps)

transform: the free superpower

transform moves/scales/rotates WITHOUT triggering layout — the GPU handles it at 60fps.

CODE  ·  Transform cookbook
.lift:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); }       /* hover lift */
.zoom:hover img { transform: scale(1.05); }        /* image zoom (parent overflow:hidden) */
.spin:hover { transform: rotate(180deg); }         /* icon flip */
.center-abs { transform: translate(-50%, -50%); }  /* dead-center trick */
.flip { transform: scaleX(-1); }                   /* mirror (RTL icons!) */
.tilt { transform: perspective(600px) rotateX(8deg); }  /* 3D card tilt */

keyframes: full choreography

CODE  ·  A professional loader + entrance reveal
.loader { width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: 50%;
  border: 4px solid #e2e8f0; border-top-color: navy;
  animation: spin 0.8s linear infinite; }
@keyframes spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } }

.reveal { animation: rise 0.6s ease-out both; }
@keyframes rise {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(24px); }
  to   { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
}
.stagger > *:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 0.1s; }
.stagger > *:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: 0.2s; }
Table 54 — animation shorthand: `rise 0.6s ease-out 0s 1 both`
PartMeaning
nameWhich @keyframes
duration/timing/delaySame as transition
iteration1, 3, infinite (loaders)
fill-modeboth = keep first frame before + last frame after (prevents flashes)

The 60fps rule + reduced motion

Key takeaway — Key takeaway

Animate ONLY transform and opacity. Animating width/margin/top/left forces layout+paint every frame = janky 15fps on phones. When in doubt: transform: translate() instead of top/left, scale() instead of width/height.

CODE  ·  Respect users who disable motion (vestibular disorders)
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; }
}
Quick check — Smoothest hover lift?
  1. margin-top:-4px
  2. top:-4px
  3. transform:translateY(-4px)
  4. padding change
Answer: C  ·  transform runs on the GPU compositor; the rest trigger layout/paint every frame.
Exercise 19 — Animated card gallery

Cards fade-rise on load (staggered), images zoom on hover, button lifts. All 60fps-safe + reduced-motion fallback.

Solution

.card{animation:rise .5s ease-out both} img{transition:transform .4s} .card:hover img{transform:scale(1.06)} + stagger delays + the reduced-motion block above. Only transform/opacity animated — DevTools Performance shows steady 60fps.

Custom properties: design tokens

CODE  ·  One source of truth for the whole design
:root {
  --brand: #2563eb; --brand-dark: #1e40af; --gold: #c9a227;
  --ink: #1c2333; --muted: #64748b; --bg: #ffffff; --card: #f8fafc;
  --radius: 12px; --space: 1rem; --shadow: 0 10px 30px rgb(2 6 23 / 0.08);
  --font: "Segoe UI", Arial, sans-serif;
}
body { font-family: var(--font); color: var(--ink); background: var(--bg); }
.btn { background: var(--brand); border-radius: var(--radius); }
/* Dark theme = reassign variables, zero rewritten rules */
[data-theme="dark"] {
  --bg: #0b1026; --card: #131a3a; --ink: #e2e8f0; --muted: #94a3b8;
}
Pro tip — var() superpowers

Fallbacks: color: var(--brand, navy). Scoping: redefine inside any selector (.card { --brand: green; } themes one card). Runtime: JavaScript can change them live (el.style.setProperty('--brand', 'red')) — the backbone of theme toggles.

BEM naming (stop class chaos)

Table 55 — BEM: Block__Element--Modifier
PartMeaningExample
BlockStandalone component.card, .nav
Element (__)Part inside block.card__title, .nav__link
Modifier (--)Variant/state.card--featured, .btn--large
CODE  ·  BEM in action
.card { … } .card__img { … } .card__title { … } .card__price { … }
.card--featured { border: 2px solid var(--gold); }
.btn--large { padding: 1rem 2rem; font-size: 1.1rem; }
Key takeaway — Key takeaway

BEM kills specificity wars: every selector is ONE flat class (0-1-0), so order decides ties and nothing fights. Readable in HTML, greppable in code, scalable to 10,000 lines.

Project: responsive landing page (90 min)

NAV (sticky): logo + links + CTA button HERO: headline + sub + 2 buttons + hero image (grid 2col → 1col) FEATURES: 3 cards (auto-fit grid) with icons PRICING: 3 plans, middle featured (flex row → wrap) TESTIMONIALS: quotes slider-look (grid) — static, no JS yet CTA + FOOTER: big call-to-action + link columns
Figure 10 — Landing page blueprint
CODE  ·  Landing core (theme + layout + components)
:root { --brand: #2563eb; --ink: #16225c; --bg: #fff; --radius: 14px; }
.container { width: 100%; max-width: 1120px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 20px; }
.site-nav { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 50; background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.9); backdrop-filter: blur(8px); }

Add data-theme="dark" styles for your landing page: dark bg, light ink, softer shadows. Toggle by editing the <html> tag manually for now — Chapter 29 wires it to a button with JavaScript.

CSS Datasheet — Every Important Property in One Place

In this chapter

DatasheetW3Schools refMDN ref
Table 56 — Specificity & cascade (memorize)
SelectorScoreNotes
p0-0-1Elements weakest
.card0-1-0Classes: your daily tool
#nav1-0-0Beats any number of classes
style=""TopInline (avoid)
!importantNuclearUtilities/third-party only
box-sizingBox
border-box makes width include padding+border (sane). Apply universally.
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
key: First rule of every professional stylesheet.
margin / paddingBox
Outside gap / inside space. Clock shorthand: top right bottom left.
.card { margin: 0 auto 24px; padding: 20px 24px; }
key: Vertical margins collapse; use gap in flex/grid instead.
border / border-radiusBox
Edge line (width style color) and corner rounding.
.btn { border: 2px solid navy; border-radius: 999px; }
key: 999px = capsule; 50% + square = circle.
width / max-widthSizing
Fixed width vs fluid-with-ceiling. The container pattern uses both.
.container { width: 100%; max-width: 1100px; margin: 0 auto; }
key: Fixed widths break phones; max-width never does.
height / min-heightSizing
Rigid height (overflows text!) vs elastic minimum that grows.
.hero { min-height: 80vh; } .card { min-height: 200px; }
key: Never fix height on text containers.
font-size / font-weightTypography
Letter scale (rem!) vs stroke thickness (100–900).
body { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 400; }
h1 { font-size: 3rem; font-weight: 800; }
key: Size = zoom; weight = pen thickness. Different universes.
line-heightTypography
Line spacing. Unitless multiplies each element's own font-size.
body { line-height: 1.6; } h1 { line-height: 1.1; }
key: Unitless always; px line-height squashes headings.
color / opacityColor
Text color; opacity fades whole element (children included).
.muted { color: #64748b; } .ghost { opacity: 0.5; }
key: Prefer rgb alpha for backgrounds (opacity hits children).
backgroundBackground
Shorthand: color image position/size repeat. Gradients stack over images.
.hero { background: linear-gradient(rgb(0 0 0 / .5), rgb(0 0 0 / .5)), url(h.jpg) center/cover; }
key: background is really background-image + color + friends.
displayLayout
block (row) / inline (text flow) / inline-block / none / flex / grid.
img.c { display: block; margin: auto; } .x { display: none; }
key: display:none removes from layout AND screen readers.
positionLayout
static / relative (anchor) / absolute (to anchor) / fixed (viewport) / sticky (hybrid).
.card { position: relative; } .badge { position: absolute; top: 8px; right: 8px; }
key: Absolute needs a positioned ancestor or it flies to the page.
flex containerFlexbox
display:flex + direction + main-axis (justify) + cross-axis (align) + gap + wrap.
.row { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; gap: 16px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
key: justify = main axis; align = cross axis.
flex itemFlexbox
flex: grow shrink basis. flex:1 eats space; 0 0 260px stays fixed.
.side { flex: 0 0 260px; } .main { flex: 1; }
key: Basis = starting size; grow = share of leftovers.
grid containerGrid
display:grid + column/row tracks + gap. auto-fit+minmax = responsive with zero queries.
.g { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(240px, 1fr)); gap: 20px; }
key: fr = fraction of free space.
grid placementGrid
Place by line numbers (2/4) or named areas. span N takes N tracks.
.big { grid-column: 1 / 3; } .tall { grid-row: span 2; }
key: Lines are boundaries BETWEEN tracks, starting at 1.
media queriesResponsive
min-width layers enhancements upward (mobile-first).
@media (min-width: 768px) { .layout { grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr; } }
key: Breakpoints follow content pain, not device names.
clamp()Responsive
Fluid value with floor and ceiling. Perfect for type.
h1 { font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 1rem + 4vw, 3.5rem); }
key: MIN, preferred-fluid, MAX — never unbounded vw.
transitionMotion
Smooth A→B: property duration timing delay.
.btn { transition: background .25s ease, transform .25s ease; }
key: 150–300ms; list properties (never bare "all" in hot UI).
transformMotion
GPU move/scale/rotate without layout cost.
.card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px) scale(1.01); }
key: The only layout-safe motion (with opacity).
animationMotion
keyframes choreography: name duration timing delay count fill.
.pop { animation: rise .5s ease-out both; }
@keyframes rise { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(20px); } }
key: fill "both" prevents pre/post flashes.
CSS variablesArchitecture
Custom properties: single source of truth + runtime theming.
:root { --brand: #2563eb; } .btn { background: var(--brand, navy); }
key: var() accepts a fallback second argument.

Values and types (only 8 exist)

Table 58 — The 8 JavaScript types

CODE  ·  Types in the console — try each line

Think of it like this — Types are labeled jars

A variable is a jar; its type is the label. JavaScript jars are magic: the same jar can hold a number now and a string later (dynamic typing). Powerful — but you must always know WHAT is inside before operating (hence typeof and careful checks).

Strings: quotes, escape, template literals

Key takeaway — Key takeaway

Default to template literals (backticks) for any string with variables: ` Hello ${name} beats "Hello " + name` in readability and safety. Use quotes only for short fixed text.

Exercise 21 — Console calculator

In the console: compute a 15% tip on 240, build the string "Total: 276" with a template literal, and print both with ONE console.log. Then check each value's typeof.

Solution

const bill = 240, tip = bill * 0.15, total = bill + tip; console.log(Tip: ${tip}, Total: ${total}); → "Tip: 36, Total: 276". typeof total = "number". You just did variables + math + strings in 2 lines.

Chapter 24

Variables and Memory — let, const, var and the Truth About Copying

Beginner+~ 100 min
Declaring variables correctly, understanding where values live, and why objects "copy weird".
In this chapter
  • let vs const vs var (and why var is retired)
  • Naming rules
  • Primitives vs references (stack vs heap)

  • const objects can still change inside!
Elzero JS #16–#30Gamal JS #9–#15MDN JS

let vs const vs var

Table 59 — The only variable table you need
KeywordScopeReassign?Redeclare?Verdict
constBlock {}NONODEFAULT for everything
letBlock {}YesNOOnly when reassignment is required
varFunction (leaks!)YesYes (silently!)RETIRED — never write in new code
CODE  ·  const-first thinking
const PI = 3.14159;
const user = { name: "Sara" };   // const = the BINDING never changes…
user.name = "Omar";              // …but the object's insides CAN change ✔
let score = 0;
score = 95;                      // let = reassignment expected ✔
// var x = 1;                    // ✘ retired: function scope + hoisting weirdness
Key takeaway — Key takeaway

const by default, let when you must reassign, var never. This single habit prevents an entire class of bugs (accidental overwrites) and signals intent to every reader: "this name always means this thing."

Naming rules (machines + humans)

CODE  ·  Names that professionals respect
const userName = "sara";     // camelCase for variables/functions ✔
const MAX_RETRIES = 3;       // SCREAMING_SNAKE for true constants ✔
let isLoggedIn = false;      // booleans ask questions: is/has/can ✔
const userCount = 5;         // nouns + units, never x1, tmp, data2 ✔
// const 2fast = 1;           // ✘ cannot start with digit
// const user-name = 1;       // ✘ dash = minus! use camelCase

Primitives vs references (the big mental model)

PRIMITIVES ............ copy the VALUE (independent twins) let a = 5; let b = a; b = 99; --> a is STILL 5 ✔ REFERENCES ............ copy the POINTER (two names, ONE object) const o1 = {n: 5}; const o2 = o1; o2.n = 99; --> o1.n is 99!
Figure 11 — Stack (primitives, copied by VALUE) vs Heap (objects, shared by REFERENCE)
CODE  ·  See it happen
let a = 5, b = a; b = 99;
console.log(a);              // 5 — independent ✔

const o1 = { n: 5 }, o2 = o1;
o2.n = 99;
console.log(o1.n);           // 99 — SHARED! o2 is a shortcut, not a copy

const arr1 = [1, 2], arr2 = arr1;
arr2.push(3);
console.log(arr1);           // [1, 2, 3] — shared again!
Think of it like this — Primitives are photocopies, objects are shared docs

Copying a number hands you an independent photocopy. Copying an object sends you a Google-Docs LINK — edits appear for everyone holding the link. Real copying needs explicit tools (spread, structuredClone — Chapter 28).

The Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) in 60 seconds

let/const exist in their block but are unusable before their declaration line — touching them throws ReferenceError. This forbidden window is the TDZ. (var instead silently gives undefined — one more reason it retired.)

CODE  ·  TDZ vs var weirdness
console.log(x);  // undefined (var hoists the declaration, not the value)
var x = 1;

console.log(y);  // ReferenceError: Cannot access 'y' before initialization
let y = 2;
Quick check — After const a=[1]; const b=a; b.push(2), a is…
  1. [1]
  2. [1,2]
  3. Error (const!)
  4. undefined
Answer: B  ·  const locks the binding (b always = that array), not the contents; a and b share one array.
Exercise 22 — Freeze the bug

A function receives settings object and accidentally changes the caller's copy. Explain why, and name TWO ways to protect the original (details in Ch 28).

Solution

Objects pass by reference — the parameter points at the caller's object. Protect via (1) spread copy {...settings} / [...arr] for shallow copies, (2) structuredClone(obj) for deep copies. Rule: never mutate inputs you don't own.

Chapter 25

Operators, Conditions and Loops

Beginner+~ 120 min
Decisions and repetition: the two superpowers that turn values into programs.
In this chapter

Elzero JS #31–#55Gamal JS #16–#28Angela §JS Logic

Arithmetic and precedence

CODE  ·  Math that bites
2 + 3 * 4        // 14 — * before + (school rules apply)
(2 + 3) * 4      // 20 — parentheses win
10 % 3           // 1 — remainder (odd/even, cycling, pagination!)
2 ** 3           // 8 — power (2³)
let n = 5;
n++              // 6 (postfix: use THEN add) vs ++n (add THEN use)
"5" + 3          // "53" — + with a string CONCATENATES!
"5" - 3          // 2 — -, *, / coerce strings to numbers
Warning — + is two-faced

+ means ADD for numbers but GLUE for strings — and ONE string converts the whole chain: 1 + 2 + "3" = "33", but "1" + 2 + 3 = "123". Mixed-type + is the #1 source of "my total is 11050 instead of 60" bugs. Convert first: Number(x) + y.

=== vs == (memorize one rule)

Table 60 — Loose == (coercion chaos) vs strict === (sanity)
Expression=====Lesson
0 == "0"truefalse== converts types silently
0 == falsetruefalseFalsy cross-talk
"" == 0truefalseEmpty string = zero?!
null == undefinedtruefalseThe ONLY sane == case
CODE  ·  The professional rule: === everywhere, always
if (role === "admin") { … }   // type AND value must match ✔
// if (role == "admin")        // ✘ coercion roulette — banned in this book

The 8 falsy values (everything else is truthy): false, 0, -0, 0n, "", null, undefined, NaN. Memorize via: "false, zero, empty string, null, undefined, NaN".

Conditions: if, ternary, switch

CODE  ·  Choosing cleanly
const age = 20;
if (age >= 18) { console.log("Adult"); }
else if (age >= 13) { console.log("Teen"); }
else { console.log("Child"); }

// Ternary: value-IF in one line (assigning or returning only!)
const fee = age >= 18 ? 100 : 50;

// switch: MANY exact matches on one value
const day = "sat";
switch (day) {
  case "sat": case "sun": console.log("Weekend"); break;
  case "fri": console.log("Almost!"); break;
  default: console.log("Workday");
}
Pro tip — Ternary discipline

Ternaries are for VALUES (const x = c ? a : b), never for actions (c ? doA() : doB() — use if/else). Nested ternaries (a ? b : c ? d : e) are unreadable — banned in professional code.

Logical operators: && || ?? ?.

CODE  ·  The four guards
const name = input || "Guest";        // || falls back on ANY falsy ("" 0 null…)
const qty = input ?? 1;               // ?? falls back ONLY on null/undefined ✔
user && user.logout();                // && runs right side only if left truthy
const city = user?.address?.city;      // ?. stops safely (undefined, no crash)

// Real-world combo: safe + default
const cityName = user?.address?.city ?? "Unknown";
Table 61 — || vs ?? (the interview favorite)
Input`input"G"`input ?? "G"Why it matters
"Sara"SaraSara—
"" (cleared field)G ✘"" ✔Empty string is VALID input!
0 (quantity)G ✘0 ✔Zero is VALID data!
null/undefinedGGBoth fall back

Loops: for, while, break, continue

CODE  ·  Loops complete
for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { console.log("Round", i); }

const cart = ["milk", "bread", "eggs"];
for (const item of cart) { console.log(item); }   // of = VALUES (arrays ✔)

const user = { name: "Sara", age: 30 };
for (const key in user) { console.log(key, user[key]); }  // in = KEYS (objects)

let tries = 0;
while (tries < 3) { tries++; }         // unknown iterations (retry, read lines)

for (let n = 1; n <= 10; n++) {
  if (n % 2 === 0) continue;           // skip evens
  if (n > 7) break;                    // stop entirely
  console.log(n);                      // 1 3 5 7
}
Key takeaway — Key takeaway

for...of = array VALUES. for...in = object KEYS (never for arrays — it yields string indexes + surprises). Classic for = counting/index control. while = "until something happens".

Quick check — 0 ?? "backup" gives…
  1. backup
  2. 0
  3. Error
  4. undefined
Answer: B  ·  ?? only replaces null/undefined; 0 is real data and survives. (
Exercise 23 — FizzBuzz + guards (the classic interview)

Print 1–30: "Fizz" for multiples of 3, "Buzz" for 5, "FizzBuzz" for both. Then write displayName(user) returning user?.name ?? "Guest".

Solution

Loop 1..30; check i%15===0 FIRST (both), then 3, then 5: order matters because 15 passes all three tests. const displayName = u => u?.name ?? "Guest"; — safe navigation + nullish default in one line.

Functions, Scope and Closures — The Heart of JavaScript

Intermediate~ 150 min
Reusable actions, who-sees-what rules, functions that remember, and the this keyword finally demystified.
In this chapter

Elzero JS #56–#90Gamal JS #29–#45Angela §Functions

Three ways to write functions

CODE  ·  Declaration vs expression vs arrow
// 1. Declaration: hoisted, named, the classic
function add(a, b) { return a + b; }

// 2. Expression: stored in a variable, NOT hoisted
const multiply = function (a, b) { return a * b; };

// 3. Arrow: short + inherits `this` (details below)
const square = n => n * n;
const greet = name => `Hello, ${name}!`;
const getUser = id => ({ id, name: "Sara" });  // ({}) = return an object!

console.log(add(2, 3));       // 5
console.log(square(4));       // 16
Table 62 — Which function when
FormUse for
function name()Top-level reusable logic, event handlers needing this
const f = () =>Callbacks (map/filter), short utilities, methods not using this
Methods obj.m() {}Object behaviors (keep this = the object)

Parameters: defaults, rest, destructuring preview

CODE  ·  Professional parameters
function price(qty = 1, rate = 100) { return qty * rate; }  // defaults
price();              // 100 — defaults kick in for undefined
price(3);             // 300

function sum(...nums) { return nums.reduce((a, n) => a + n, 0); }  // rest: all into array
sum(1, 2, 3, 4);      // 10

// arguments object exists but is retired — rest params replaced it.
Warning — Defaults = undefined ONLY

price(0) uses 0 (NOT the default) — defaults trigger only on undefined. Same spirit as ??. Passing null also keeps null. Design APIs accordingly.

Scope chain + closures (with REAL uses)

CODE  ·  Scope: inner sees outer, never reverse
const shop = "Roastly";
function order(item) {
  const id = Math.random();        // order() locals…
  function receipt() {
    return `${shop}: ${item} #${id}`;  // …visible here (chain upward ✔)
  }
  return receipt();
}
// console.log(id);  // ✘ ReferenceError — outside cannot see inside

A closure = a function + the variables it captured from its birthplace. It REMEMBERS them forever:

CODE  ·  Closures doing real jobs
// Job 1: private state (a counter nobody can corrupt)
function createCounter() {
  let count = 0;                          // PRIVATE — unreachable from outside
  return {
    up: () => ++count,
    down: () => --count,
    value: () => count
  };
}
const c = createCounter();
c.up(); c.up(); console.log(c.value());   // 2 (c.count is undefined — truly private!)

// Job 2: configuration factories (one maker, many behaviors)
const greeter = greeting => name => `${greeting}, ${name}!`;
const sayHi = greeter("Hi"), sayWelcome = greeter("Welcome");
sayHi("Sara");        // "Hi, Sara!"

// Job 3: event handlers remembering their data (Ch 30 uses this daily)
function handleDelete(id) {
  return () => fetch(`/api/items/${id}`, { method: "DELETE" });
}
button.onclick = handleDelete(42);  // remembers 42 until clicked
Think of it like this — Closure = function with a backpack

When a function is born inside another scope, it packs a backpack with the variables around it and carries it everywhere — even after the outer function finished and left. createCounter's count lives in the backpack, invisible to the world, usable by the returned functions.

Hoisting truth (30 seconds, no myths)

Table 63 — What hoists
DeclarationHoisted?Usable before?
function f() {}Whole functionYes (entire body available)
var xDeclaration only (= undefined)Silently undefined (bug factory)
let/constInto TDZ (locked)NO — ReferenceError
CODE  ·  Only declarations enjoy hoisting
sayHi();                    // works! (declaration hoisted whole)
function sayHi() { return "hi"; }
// sayBye();                // ✘ TypeError — const arrow sits in TDZ
const sayBye = () => "bye";

this in 5 rules (the demystification)

Table 64 — `this` = HOW the function was CALLED (4 rules + arrow exception)
Call stylethis isExample
Method: obj.m()The object before the dotuser.greet() → user
Alone: f()undefined (strict) / window (sloppy)Never rely on this!
new F()The fresh instancenew Cart() → the new cart
.call/.apply/.bindWhatever you passf.call(timer) → timer
Arrow =>NO own this — inherits enclosingCallbacks keep outer this ✔
CODE  ·  this, proven
const user = {
  name: "Sara",
  hi() { return `Hi, I'm ${this.name}`; },       // method: this = user ✔
  late() { setTimeout(function () {
    console.log(this.name);                       // ✘ undefined! plain call inside timeout
  }, 0); },
  fixed() { setTimeout(() => {
    console.log(this.name);                       // ✔ "Sara" — arrow inherits fixed()'s this
  }, 0); }
};
user.hi(); user.fixed();
Key takeaway — Key takeaway

Default to arrows for callbacks (they preserve your this), methods for objects (they receive it), and NEVER use this in standalone functions. 95% of this bugs vanish with these three habits.

Interview question — What is a closure? Give a real use.

Expected: "A function bundled with its lexical scope, so it remembers outer variables after the outer function returns. Real uses: private state like counters, factory functions, and event handlers that remember their data." Then write createCounter from memory.

Quick check — Arrow functions and this:
  1. Own this per call
  2. Inherit enclosing this, never their own
  3. Always window
  4. Always undefined
Answer: B  ·  Arrows capture this lexically at creation — that's why callbacks love them.
Exercise 24 — Secure vault

Write createVault(pin) returning {deposit(n), withdraw(n, pin), balance(pin)} where money is unreachable except with the right PIN, and wrong PIN throws.

Solution

function createVault(pin){let m=0;const ok=p=>{if(p!==pin)throw new Error("Wrong PIN")};return{deposit:n=>m+=n,withdraw:(n,p)=>{ok(p);if(n>m)throw new Error("Low funds");m-=n;return m},balance:p=>{ok(p);return m}}} — closure privacy + guard clause, the professional combo.

Chapter 27

Arrays — Ordered Data and the Methods That Rule Them

Intermediate~ 120 min
The list type behind carts, feeds and tables — plus map/filter/reduce fluency.
In this chapter
  • Creating and indexing
  • push/pop/shift/unshift/splice/slice
  • map/filter/reduce/find/some/every

Elzero JS #91–#120Gamal JS #46–#60Angela §Arrays

Create, read, and the index trap

CODE  ·  Array basics
const cart = ["milk", "bread", "eggs"];
cart[0];            // "milk" — indexes start at 0!
cart[cart.length - 1];  // "eggs" — last item pattern
cart[99];           // undefined — NO error (silent! validate indexes)
cart.length;        // 3
Warning — Off-by-one + silent undefined

arr[arr.length] is ALWAYS undefined (last index = length−1), and JS won't warn you. Every "cannot read property of undefined" crash downstream starts here. Guard: check i < arr.length or use methods that can't overrun (map/for...of).

Mutating vs non-mutating (the safety line)

Table 65 — Array methods by danger
Mutates original (think twice)Returns NEW (safe default)
push/pop (end), shift/unshift (start)map (transform each)
splice (cut/paste anywhere)filter (keep some)
sort, reverse (in place!)slice (copy part), concat, toSorted (new)
CODE  ·  Mutation vs purity, side by side
const nums = [3, 1, 2];
nums.push(4);            // nums = [3,1,2,4] (changed!)
const doubled = nums.map(n => n * 2);   // NEW [6,2,4,8], nums untouched ✔
const top2 = [...nums].sort((a, b) => b - a).slice(0, 2);  // copy-then-sort!
Key takeaway — Key takeaway

Default to non-mutating methods (map/filter/slice) — functions that don't surprise their callers. Mutate only local arrays you own (inside one function), and modern toSorted()/toReversed()/toSpliced() give sorted copies without touching originals.

The big six: map/filter/reduce/find/some/every

CODE  ·  One dataset, six questions answered
const products = [
  { id: 1, name: "Mug",   price: 120, stock: 5 },
  { id: 2, name: "Beans", price: 350, stock: 0 },
  { id: 3, name: "Press", price: 900, stock: 2 },
];
products.map(p => `${p.name} ($${p.price})`);        // transform → string list
products.filter(p => p.stock > 0);                   // keep → in-stock only
products.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.price * p.stock, 0);  // combine → 2400 (stock value)
products.find(p => p.id === 2);                      // first match → Beans (or undefined!)
products.some(p => p.stock === 0);                   // any? → true
products.every(p => p.price > 0);                    // all? → true
Table 66 — Return-value cheat-sheet
MethodReturnsEmpty-array gotcha
mapNEW array, same length[] (safe)
filterNEW array, 0..n items[] (safe)
reduceONE value (you choose)THROWS without initial value — always pass , 0!
findFirst match or undefinedundefined (check before use!)
some/everybooleanfalse / true respectively
forEachundefined (actions only)— (use for effects, never for building data)

Chaining like a senior

CODE  ·  Read it as a sentence: "in-stock → names → top 3 → display"
const topNames = products
  .filter(p => p.stock > 0)
  .sort((a, b) => b.price - a.price)
  .slice(0, 3)
  .map(p => p.name.toUpperCase());
// ["PRESS", "MUG"]

// Numeric sort needs a comparator! Default sort is ALPHABETIC:
[10, 9, 80].sort();                    // [10, 80, 9] ✘ strings!
[10, 9, 80].sort((a, b) => a - b);     // [9, 10, 80] ✔ numbers
Pro tip — forEach vs map discipline

Building data → map. Doing effects (log, save, draw) → forEach. Using forEach + outer push to build arrays is junior style — map/filter say the intent in their names.

Spread, destructure, copy right

CODE  ·  Modern array handling
const a = [1, 2], b = [3, 4];
const all = [...a, ...b, 5];      // [1,2,3,4,5] — merge + append
const [first, second] = a;        // first=1, second=2
const copy = [...a];              // shallow copy (top level only!)
copy.push(99);                    // a untouched ✔
// Nested objects still shared — structuredClone for deep copies (Ch 28).
Quick check — [3,1,2].sort() gives…
  1. [1,2,3]
  2. [1,3,2]
  3. [3,1,2]
  4. Error
Answer: A  ·  Single digits sort fine either way — the trap needs 2-digit numbers ([10,9,80]→[10,80,9]). Always pass comparators for numbers regardless.
Exercise 25 — Cart total + receipt

From cart = [{name, price, qty}…]: (1) filter qty>0, (2) map to line strings "Mug ×2 = 240", (3) reduce to grand total. One chain + one reduce.

Solution

const lines = cart.filter(i => i.qty > 0).map(i => ${i.name} ×${i.qty} = ${i.pricei.qty}); const total = cart.reduce((s, i) => s + i.pricei.qty, 0); — filter→map builds display, reduce computes money. Note reduce's , 0 guard.

Objects: named data + behavior

CODE  ·  An object is a labeled drawer set
const product = {
  name: "Mug",
  price: 120,
  stock: 5,
  sell(n = 1) {                       // method shorthand (this = product)
    if (n > this.stock) throw new Error("Not enough stock");
    this.stock -= n;
    return this.stock;
  }
};
product.name;          // "Mug" (dot = known key)
product["pro" + "duct"] // dynamic keys via brackets
"name" in product;     // true — existence check
delete product.stock;  // remove a key (rare — prefer building new objects)

Destructuring + spread (daily professional syntax)

CODE  ·  Unpack exactly what you need
const user = { id: 7, name: "Sara", role: "admin", city: "Cairo" };
const { name, role = "user" } = user;         // name="Sara", default if missing
const { city: town } = user;                  // rename: town="Cairo"
const { id, ...publicData } = user;           // rest: everything except id

function welcome({ name, role = "user" }) {   // destructure PARAMETERS
  return `${name} (${role})`;
}
CODE  ·  Spread builds new objects (immutability pattern)
const updated = { ...user, city: "Alex" };     // copy + override city
const merged = { ...defaults, ...options };    // options win (order matters!)
// Shallow only: nested objects still shared. Deep? structuredClone(obj).
const deep = structuredClone(user);
Table 67 — Copy depths (the whole story)
ToolDepthUse
{...o} / [...a]Shallow (top level)Flat updates, React state
structuredClone(o)Deep (everything)Nested data, no functions inside
JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(o))Deep-ish legacyOnly if structuredClone unavailable (loses dates/functions)

JSON: objects as text

CODE  ·  Talking to servers and storage
const json = JSON.stringify(user);     // object → '{"id":7,…}' (send/store)
const back = JSON.parse(json);         // text → object (receive/load)
JSON.stringify(user, null, 2);         // pretty-print with 2-space indent
Warning — JSON is stricter than JS

Keys MUST be double-quoted, no trailing commas, no functions/undefined/comments. JSON.parse throws on bad text — always wrap real-world parsing in try/catch (Chapter 34).

Prototypes in 5 minutes (then classes forever)

Every object has a hidden link to a prototype it inherits from. Arrays share Array.prototype (that's where map lives!); all objects share Object.prototype (toString, hasOwnProperty). Lookup climbs the chain until found or null.

CODE  ·  The chain in action
const arr = [1, 2];
arr.map;              // found on Array.prototype (shared by ALL arrays ✔ memory-efficient)
arr.toString;         // found higher, on Object.prototype
// Classes below are CLEAN SYNTAX over this same prototype system.

Classes + private fields + modules

CODE  ·  A professional class (bank account)
class Account {
  #balance = 0;                            // truly private (outside CANNOT touch)
  constructor(owner) { this.owner = owner; }
  deposit(n) {
    if (n <= 0) throw new Error("Amount must be positive");
    this.#balance += n;
    return this.#balance;
  }
  get balance() { return this.#balance; }  // read-only view
  static bankName() { return "Nile Bank"; } // on the class, not instances
}
const me = new Account("Sara");
me.deposit(500); me.balance;               // 500 (me.#balance = syntax error outside!)
CODE  ·  Modules — split code across files (modern standard)
// math.js
export const add = (a, b) => a + b;
export default class Calc { /* … */ }
// app.js
import Calc, { add } from "./math.js";
const lazy = await import("./heavy-charts.js");  // load ONLY when needed ✔
Table 68 — Module rules
RuleMeaning
export / export defaultShare from a file (many named, one default)
import … fromReceive in another file (paths need ./ + .js)
<script type="module">Browser entry point (deferred + strict automatically)
Dynamic import()Lazy-load heavy features on demand
Interview question — Shallow vs deep copy?

Expected: "Spread copies top-level only — nested objects stay shared. structuredClone copies everything. I use spread for flat state updates and structuredClone for nested data." Bonus: mention JSON trick loses Dates/functions.

Exercise 26 — Safe settings updater

update(settings, patch) returns a NEW object with patch applied, original untouched — including one nested level (theme: {…}).

Solution

const update = (s, p) => ({ ...s, ...p, theme: { ...s.theme, ...p.theme } }); — top spread + manual nested spread. For unknown depth, structuredClone(s) then Object.assign(clone, p).

The DOM tree (HTML as live objects)

<body> body (Element) <h1 id="t">Hi</h1> ---> |-- h1#t (Element) <p>Text</p> : |-- "Hi" (Text node) +-- p (Element) +-- "Text" (Text node) document = the root. EVERYTHING hangs below it. JS edits objects → browser repaints.

Selecting elements (the 4 you need)

CODE  ·  Selection mastery

const cards = document.querySelectorAll(".card");  // ALL matches (static NodeList)
const byId = document.getElementById("t");         // fastest single lookup

NeedUse
One element, any selectorquerySelector("#x .y")

textContent vs innerHTML (read before touching!)

CODE  ·  The safety line of the DOM
name.textContent = userInput;      // ✔ SAFE: inserts pure TEXT ("<b>" shows literally)
box.innerHTML = `<b>${total}</b>`; // ⚠ HTML parsed — NEVER with untrusted input (XSS!)

// Building safely with user data:

li.textContent = comment;          // user text CANNOT become executable HTML ✔

Warning — innerHTML + user input = hacked site

box.innerHTML = comment where comment = <img src=x onerror="steal()"> RUNS the attacker's code in every visitor's browser (XSS). Rule: textContent for user data; innerHTML only for YOUR OWN static templates — and even then prefer createElement.

Create, insert, remove, clone

CODE  ·  DOM surgery complete
const li = document.createElement("li");
li.className = "item";
li.dataset.id = "42";              // → <li data-id="42"> (dataset API!)
li.textContent = "New item";

list.append(li);                   // end … prepend(start), before/after(siblings)
list.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend", "<li>Fast static row</li>");  // fastest for YOUR html
li.remove();                       // delete (modern — no parent needed)
const copy = card.cloneNode(true); // deep clone (listeners NOT copied)

// Zero-reflow batch rendering (500 rows, no jank):
const frag = document.createDocumentFragment();
items.forEach(t => { const el = document.createElement("li"); el.textContent = t; frag.append(el); });
list.append(frag);                 // ONE layout instead of 500 ✔

PositionMeaning
beforebeginBefore the element itself (sibling)
afterbeginFirst child
beforeendLast child (append HTML)
afterendAfter the element itself (sibling)

Classes, styles, attributes

Key takeaway — Key takeaway

Style via CLASSES (CSS owns design), touch el.style only for truly dynamic values (drag positions, progress widths). Toggle UI states with classList.toggle + CSS doing the visuals.

Quick check — Rendering 1000 rows fastest?
  1. innerHTML in a loop
  2. append one-by-one
  3. DocumentFragment batch
  4. alert() each
Answer: C  ·  Fragment builds off-screen with zero layouts, then commits once. innerHTML-once is runner-up for trusted static HTML.
Exercise 27 — Live search filter

Input filters a <ul> of 50 names as you type (hide non-matches). No innerHTML with the query!

Table 71 — Everyday events
CategoryEventse.target gives you
Mouseclick dblclick mouseenter mouseleaveClicked element
Keyboardkeydown keyup (+ e.key: "Enter", "Escape"…)Focused element

CODE  ·  Keyboard + form patterns
input.addEventListener("keydown", e => {
  if (e.key === "Enter") search(e.target.value);
  if (e.key === "Escape") e.target.blur();
});

  e.preventDefault();              // STOP page reload — handle with JS ✔
  save(new FormData(form));        // all fields as data object!

Bubbling: events float upward

<button>Delete</button> ← click starts HERE (target phase) ↑ bubbles: <li> → <ul id="list"> → <main> → <body> → document → window A listener on <ul> HEARS clicks from every <li>/<button> inside it! (Capturing = the reverse trip down; default listeners use bubbling.)
Figure 13 — Click ripples UP the tree (bubbling)
CODE  ·  One listener, infinite buttons (THE delegation pattern)
document.querySelector("#list").addEventListener("click", e => {
  const btn = e.target.closest("button[data-act]");  // find the real button
  if (!btn) return;                                  // clicked elsewhere — ignore
  const id = btn.closest("li").dataset.id;
  if (btn.dataset.act === "del") deleteItem(id);
  if (btn.dataset.act === "edit") editItem(id);
});
Think of it like this — Delegation = one doorman

Instead of a guard at every office door (500 listeners = memory + re-binding new rows), post ONE doorman at the building entrance who asks "which office?" (closest()). New offices (dynamically added rows) work instantly — the doorman was already there.

Table 72 — When delegation wins
CaseWhy
Lists/tables with many rows1 listener vs N; new rows work free
Dynamically added contentNo re-binding after every render
Memory + simplicityFewer closures, one place to debug
CODE  ·  Full delegation example (todo list: toggle + delete)
<ul id="todos">
  <li data-id="1">Milk <button data-act="done">✔</button> <button data-act="del">✘</button></li>
</ul>
<script>
document.querySelector("#todos").addEventListener("click", e => {
  const btn = e.target.closest("button");
  if (!btn) return;
  const li = btn.closest("li");
  if (btn.dataset.act === "done") li.classList.toggle("done");
  if (btn.dataset.act === "del") li.remove();
});
</script>
Interview question — How would you handle clicks on 1000 table rows?

Expected: "Event delegation — one listener on the <tbody>, use event.target.closest() to find the row and its data-id. It uses constant memory and automatically covers rows added later." Mention bubbling as the mechanism.

Quick check — e.target vs e.currentTarget:
  1. Same thing
  2. target = clicked element, currentTarget = listener's element
  3. Reversed
  4. Both window
Answer: B  ·  With delegation they differ constantly: target is the button, currentTarget the list. Confusing them breaks delegation.

Grid of 12 thumbnails; ONE listener opens the clicked full image in a modal; Escape or backdrop-click closes; focus returns to the thumbnail.

Grid listener: const img = e.target.closest("img"); if (!img) return; openModal(img.dataset.full). Modal: backdrop click (e.target === backdrop) or keydown Escape closes; store lastFocus and .focus() it on close. Accessibility + performance in one pattern.

Warning — Don't write the "perfect email regex"

The RFC-valid email regex is 6,000+ characters. Use type="email" + server-side verification email instead. Regex validates SHAPE; only the server (and the inbox) validates TRUTH.

Storage: local vs session vs cookies

Table 75 — Browser storage
StoreCapacityLifetimeSent to server?Use for
localStorage~5MBForever (until cleared)NOTheme, drafts, cart, UI prefs
sessionStorage~5MBTab lifetimeNOMulti-step wizards, temp flow state

CODE  ·  Storage done right (objects need JSON!)
// localStorage stores STRINGS ONLY — stringify objects:
const save = (k, v) => localStorage.setItem(k, JSON.stringify(v));
const load = (k, fb) => {
  try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(k)) ?? fb; }
  catch { return fb; }   // corrupted data never crashes the app ✔
};
save("cart", [{ id: 1, qty: 2 }]);
const cart = load("cart", []);
Warning — NEVER store secrets in localStorage

Any XSS hole lets attackers read ALL localStorage — tokens included. Auth tokens belong in HttpOnly cookies (server-set, JS-invisible). localStorage = preferences and public data ONLY. (Full story: Chapters 43–44.)

Project: theme toggle (Chapter 21 payoff!)

CODE  ·  Dark-mode toggle in 20 lines
<button id="themeBtn" aria-pressed="false">🌙 Dark</button>
<script>
const root = document.documentElement;
const btn = document.querySelector("#themeBtn");
const apply = t => {
  root.dataset.theme = t;
  localStorage.setItem("theme", t);
  btn.textContent = t === "dark" ? "☀️ Light" : "🌙 Dark";
  btn.setAttribute("aria-pressed", t === "dark");
};
apply(localStorage.getItem("theme") || "light");   // restore saved choice
btn.addEventListener("click", () =>
  apply(root.dataset.theme === "dark" ? "light" : "dark"));
</script>

Chapter 32

Async JavaScript — The Event Loop, Promises and async/await

Advanced~ 140 min
How JS does many things on one thread: the engine's queuing system and clean async code.
In this chapter
  • Sync vs async + the event loop
  • Microtasks vs macrotasks
  • Promises + combinators
  • async/await + error handling
  • Timeouts, intervals, debounce
Elzero asyncGamal asyncAngela §Async

The event loop (JS juggles on one thread)

CALL STACK ......... runs sync code NOW (one thing at a time) | stack empty? v MICROTASK QUEUE .... ALL promise callbacks (.then/await) — VIP line, drains FULLY | microtasks empty? v RENDER ............. paint the page (60fps chance) | v MACROTASK QUEUE .... ONE task: setTimeout / setInterval / I/O / events — then loop!
Figure 14 — The loop that runs everything
CODE  ·  Predict this (the classic interview demo)
console.log("1 sync");
setTimeout(() => console.log("2 timeout"), 0);
Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log("3 promise"));
console.log("4 sync");
// Output: 1, 4, 3, 2 — promises (micro) ALWAYS beat timeouts (macro)!
Think of it like this — The event loop is a restaurant kitchen

Sync code = the dish being cooked NOW. Microtasks = VIP orders the chef finishes completely before anything else. Macrotasks = the regular ticket rail (one per round). Render = serving the table between rounds. Starving VIPs (infinite promise chains) freeze the restaurant!

Promises: receipts for future values

CODE  ·  Promise anatomy
const getUser = id => fetch(`/api/users/${id}`).then(r => {
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}`);  // fetch only rejects on NETWORK failure!
  return r.json();
});
getUser(7)
  .then(user => console.log(user.name))   // fulfilled path
  .catch(err => console.error("Failed:", err.message))  // ANY failure above lands here
  .finally(() => hideSpinner());          // always runs (cleanup!)
Warning — fetch's famous lie

fetch RESOLVES on 404/500 (it got an answer!) and rejects ONLY on network failure (offline/DNS). Always check response.ok yourself — forgetting this ships bugs that "work" while showing error pages as data.

Table 76 — Promise combinators (many async jobs)
ToolWaits forFails whenUse
Promise.allALL succeedFIRST failure (rest ignored)Dashboard needing every source
Promise.allSettledALL finishNever (reports each)Bulk imports where partial OK
Promise.raceFIRST to finishIf winner failsTimeouts racing requests
Promise.anyFIRST successALL failMirror servers / fallbacks
CODE  ·  Combinators in action
const [user, posts] = await Promise.all([getUser(7), getPosts(7)]);  // parallel = fast ✔
// Sequential await in a loop = SLOW (each waits). Parallel array + all = FAST.

async/await (write async like sync)

CODE  ·  The professional async function template
async function loadDashboard(id) {
  showSpinner();
  const ctrl = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), 8000);   // 8s timeout ✔
  try {
    const res = await fetch(`/api/dash/${id}`, { signal: ctrl.signal });
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`);
    return await res.json();
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.name === "AbortError") showToast("Request timed out — retry?");
    else showToast(`Failed: ${err.message}`);
    throw err;                       // let caller decide too
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
    hideSpinner();                   // ALWAYS cleanup
  }
}
Table 77 — async/await rules
RuleWhy
await only inside async (or top-level modules)Syntax law
Every await can throw → wrap in try/catchUnhandled rejections crash logic
Independent jobs → Promise.all (parallel)Sequential await multiplies latency
Always timeout network callsHanging spinners are UX death

Timers + debounce (search boxes done right)

CODE  ·  Debounce: wait until the user STOPS typing
const debounce = (fn, ms = 300) => {
  let t;
  return (...args) => { clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(() => fn(...args), ms); };
};
searchInput.addEventListener("input", debounce(e => searchAPI(e.target.value)));
// 10 fast keystrokes = 1 API call instead of 10 ✔ (saves servers + money)
Quick check — Output order: sync A, promise P, timeout T?
  1. A P T
  2. A T P
  3. P A T
  4. T P A
Answer: A  ·  Sync first, then microtasks (promises), then macrotasks (timeouts). The engine drains VIPs fully before one regular.

Solution

Promise.allSettled with AbortController timeout; filter fulfilled → render; rejected → collect names into retry panel. Parallel + resilient + honest UI — the senior async trifecta.

fetch CRUD (the complete set)

CODE  ·  One helper, every method (copy into projects)
async function api(path, { method = "GET", body, token } = {}) {
  const res = await fetch(`https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com${path}`, {
    method,
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "application/json",          // "my body is JSON"
      ...(token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {})
    },
    ...(body ? { body: JSON.stringify(body) } : {})
  });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return res.status === 204 ? null : res.json();   // 204 = no body!
}
// CREATE          api("/posts", { method: "POST", body: { title: "Hi" } })
// READ            api("/posts/1")
// UPDATE          api("/posts/1", { method: "PATCH", body: { title: "New" } })
// DELETE          api("/posts/1", { method: "DELETE" })
Table 78 — Request anatomy
PieceExampleJob
Method + pathPATCH /posts/1What + which
HeadersContent-Type, AuthorizationMeta-instructions about the call
BodyJSON.stringify(obj)The data (never with GET!)
Response checkres.ok + statusfetch won't do it for you!

The 4 UI states (seniors never ship 2)

Every data screen has FOUR states — juniors build two (data + nothing) and users suffer:

CODE  ·  State machine for any data view
async function renderPosts() {
  setState("loading");                       // 1. skeleton/spinner
  try {
    const posts = await api("/posts?_limit=10");
    if (!posts.length) return setState("empty");   // 2. friendly zero-state
    paint(posts); setState("ready");               // 3. data ✔
  } catch (err) {
    setState("error", err.message);                // 4. error + RETRY button
  }
}
Table 79 — The 4 states
StateShowsRookie mistake
LoadingSkeleton rows (not blank!)Blank screen = "is it broken?"
Empty"No posts yet — write the first!" + actionBlank = looks broken
ErrorWhat failed + Retry buttonconsole-only error = user stranded
ReadyThe data(the only state juniors build)

Project: posts explorer (JSONPlaceholder)

CODE  ·  Full mini-app: list + search + details (public test API, no key needed)
<input id="q" placeholder="Search posts…">
<div id="status"></div>
<ul id="posts"></ul>
<article id="detail" hidden></article>
<script>
const postsEl = document.querySelector("#posts");
const render = async () => {
  status("Loading…");
  try {
    const posts = await api("/posts?_limit=20");
    const q = document.querySelector("#q").value.toLowerCase();
    const shown = posts.filter(p => (p.title + p.body).toLowerCase().includes(q));
    postsEl.innerHTML = "";                       // own template below — safe…
    if (!shown.length) return status("No matches. Try another word.");
    const frag = document.createDocumentFragment();
    shown.forEach(p => {
      const li = document.createElement("li");
      const b = document.createElement("button");
      b.textContent = p.title; b.dataset.id = p.id;   // textContent = XSS-safe ✔
      li.append(b); frag.append(li);
    });
    postsEl.append(frag); status("");
  } catch (e) { status("Failed to load. <button id='retry'>Retry</button>"); }
};
postsEl.addEventListener("click", async e => {
  const b = e.target.closest("button"); if (!b) return;
  const post = await api(`/posts/${b.dataset.id}`);
  const d = document.querySelector("#detail");
  d.hidden = false; d.querySelector("h2").textContent = post.title;
});
const status = msg => document.querySelector("#status").innerHTML = msg;
document.querySelector("#q").addEventListener("input", debounce(render, 300));
render();
</script>
Key takeaway — Key takeaway

Real API code = helper (method/headers/ok-check) + 4 UI states + XSS-safe rendering (textContent/createElement) + debounce on search. This pattern scales from homework to production unchanged.

try/catch/finally + throwing well

CODE  ·  Errors as values, not crashes
function parseAge(input) {
  const n = Number(input);
  if (!Number.isInteger(n)) throw new TypeError(`Age must be an integer, got ${input!r}`);
  if (n < 0 || n > 130) throw new RangeError(`Age ${n} out of range 0–130`);
  return n;
}
try {
  const age = parseAge(form.age.value);
  save(age);
} catch (err) {
  console.error(err.name, err.message);   // TypeError/RangeError + context
  showFieldError("age", err.message);     // user sees FRIENDLY text
} finally {
  submitBtn.disabled = false;             // ALWAYS re-enable (success or fail)
}
Table 80 — Error types to throw
TypeMeaning
ErrorGeneric (default)
TypeErrorWrong type/shape (user.map is not a function)
RangeErrorOut of bounds (age 999)
SyntaxErrorBad text format (JSON.parse fails → catch it!)
Custom class AuthError extends ErrorDomain failures (wrong PIN, expired token)
Key takeaway — Key takeaway

Throw EARLY with SPECIFIC types + context ("Age must be integer, got 'abc'"), catch at BOUNDARIES (event handlers, API calls), and NEVER show raw errors to users (log technical, display friendly).

Debug like a senior (breakpoints > console.log spam)

Table 81 — DevTools debugging workflow
StepHow
1. Pause on errorSources → ⏸ "Pause on exceptions" (stops AT the crash!)
2. BreakpointClick a line number → reload → execution FREEZES there
3. InspectHover variables; Scope panel shows closures; Console runs live code
4. StepF10 step-over, F11 step-into functions, F8 resume
5. NetworkFailed request? Check status + response body + headers
Try it yourself — Catch a bug red-handed (5 minutes)

Paste buggy code (e.g. users.map where users is null) → Sources → enable Pause on exceptions → run → DevTools freezes ON the crash line with the full call stack. Fix in 1 minute what console.log-hunting takes 30.

Regex: validate shapes, safely

CODE  ·  Practical regex (test + patterns from Ch 31, leveled up)
const patterns = {
  username: /^[a-z0-9_]{3,16}$/i,        // i = case-insensitive
  egyptPhone: /^(\+20|0)?1[0125]\d{8}$/,
  slug: /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/,
  strongPw: /^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\d).{8,}$/
};
patterns.username.test("sara_dev");      // true
// Escape user text before embedding in regex:
const escapeRe = s => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
Warning — ReDoS: evil regex can hang servers

Nested quantifiers like (a+)+$ on long input can freeze Node for seconds (Regular-expression Denial of Service). Keep patterns simple, anchor with ^$, prefer length checks + simple classes over clever one-liners.

Quick check — Best first debugging step?
  1. Add 20 console.logs
  2. Pause on exceptions + breakpoint
  3. Rewrite the file
  4. Ask AI immediately
Answer: B  ·  Freezing AT the crash with live scope beats guessing. Logs confirm; breakpoints reveal.

Solution

The architecture (memorize this triangle)

STATE (plain JS object/array — the single truth) | mutate via functions only (addTodo, answerQuiz…) v RENDER (state → DOM via template functions + delegation) | v PERSIST (localStorage / API sync after each mutation) Events flow BACK up: user → handler → mutate state → re-render.
Figure 15 — Every front-end app, from todo to trading dashboard

Project 1 — Timed quiz with highscores

CODE  ·  Quiz: data + state machine (60 lines that teach architecture)
const QUESTIONS = [
  { q: "2 + '2' = ?", opts: ["4", "22", "NaN", "Error"], answer: 1 },
  { q: "Which copies deeply?", opts: ["{...o}", "slice()", "structuredClone", "assign"], answer: 2 },
];
const state = { i: 0, score: 0, time: 30, timer: null, lock: false };

function render() {
  const Q = QUESTIONS[state.i];
  qEl.textContent = `Q${state.i + 1}. ${Q.q}`;
  optsEl.innerHTML = "";
  Q.opts.forEach((t, idx) => {
    const li = document.createElement("li");
    const b = document.createElement("button");
    b.textContent = t; b.dataset.idx = idx; li.append(b); optsEl.append(li);
  });
  scoreEl.textContent = `Score: ${state.score} · Time: ${state.time}s`;
}
optsEl.addEventListener("click", e => {
  const b = e.target.closest("button"); if (!b || state.lock) return;
  state.lock = true;
  const correct = Number(b.dataset.idx) === QUESTIONS[state.i].answer;
  b.classList.add(correct ? "right" : "wrong");
  if (correct) state.score += 10;
  setTimeout(() => {
    state.i++; state.lock = false;
    state.i < QUESTIONS.length ? render() : finish();
  }, 600);
});
function finish() {
  clearInterval(state.timer);
  const best = Math.max(state.score, Number(localStorage.getItem("quizBest") || 0));
  localStorage.setItem("quizBest", best);
  app.innerHTML = `<h2>Done! ${state.score} pts (Best: ${best})</h2><button onclick="location.reload()">Retry</button>`;
}
state.timer = setInterval(() => { if (--state.time <= 0) finish(); else render(); }, 1000);
render();

Project 2 — Expense tracker (state + stats + bar chart by hand)

CODE  ·  Tracker core: add/delete + totals + CSS-bar chart
let items = load("expenses", []);   // [{id, label, amount, cat}]
const total = () => items.reduce((s, i) => s + i.amount, 0);
const byCat = () => items.reduce((m, i) => ((m[i.cat] ??= 0), m[i.cat] += i.amount, m), {});

function render() {
  list.innerHTML = "";
  const frag = document.createDocumentFragment();
  items.forEach(it => {
    const li = document.createElement("li");
    li.innerHTML = "";                       // build safe nodes…
    const s = document.createElement("span");
    s.textContent = `${it.label} — $${it.amount} (${it.cat})`;
    const del = document.createElement("button");
    del.textContent = "✘"; del.dataset.id = it.id; del.dataset.act = "del";
    li.append(s, del); frag.append(li);
  });
  list.append(frag);
  totalEl.textContent = `Total: $${total()}`;
  chart.innerHTML = "";
  const max = Math.max(1, ...Object.values(byCat()));
  for (const [cat, sum] of Object.entries(byCat())) {
    const bar = document.createElement("div");
    bar.className = "bar";
    bar.style.setProperty("--h", `${(sum / max) * 100}%`);
    bar.title = `${cat}: $${sum}`;
    chart.append(bar);                       // .bar{height:var(--h)} in CSS
  }
  save("expenses", items);
}
form.addEventListener("submit", e => {
  e.preventDefault();
  const d = new FormData(form);
  items.unshift({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), label: d.get("label").trim(),
    amount: Math.abs(Number(d.get("amount"))), cat: d.get("cat") });
  form.reset(); render();
});
list.addEventListener("click", e => {
  const b = e.target.closest("button[data-act='del']"); if (!b) return;
  items = items.filter(i => i.id !== b.dataset.id); render();
});
render();

JavaScript Datasheet — Methods and Syntax in One Place

Table 82 — Equality + falsy (never google again)
CheckRule
Equality=== always (== banned)
Falsy 8false, 0, -0, 0n, "", null, undefined, NaN
Default?? for null/undefined; `\\` replaces ALL falsy
Safe diveuser?.address?.city ?? "Unknown"
map / filter / reduceArrays
Transform each / keep some / combine to one. Non-mutating; chain freely.
const names = users.filter(u => u.active).map(u => u.name.toUpperCase());
const total = cart.reduce((s, i) => s + i.price * i.qty, 0);
key: reduce ALWAYS takes an initial value (empty arrays throw without it).
find / some / everyArrays
First match (or undefined) / any true? / all true?
users.find(u => u.id === 7); users.some(u => u.banned); users.every(u => u.email);
key: find returns the ITEM; some/every return booleans.
slice / spliceArrays
slice copies a range (safe); splice cuts/pastes in place (mutates!).
arr.slice(0, 3); arr.toSpliced(1, 1); // modern non-mutating
arr.splice(1, 1);                     // mutates original!
key: slice = scissors with photocopy; splice = scissors on the original.
sortArrays
In-place sort; DEFAULT IS ALPHABETIC — numbers need a comparator.
nums.sort((a, b) => a - b); users.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
key: Copy first ([...a].sort / toSorted) unless mutation is intended.
Destructuring + spreadSyntax
Unpack values; spread merges/copies (shallow).
const { name, role = "user" } = user; const next = { ...user, city: "Alex" };
key: Shallow only — nested objects stay shared (structuredClone for deep).
Template literalsStrings
Backtick strings with ${} injection + multiline.
`Hello ${name}, you have ${n} messages.`
key: Default choice for any string containing values.
String helpersStrings
The daily set: case, trim, includes, slice, split/join, replace.
s.trim().toLowerCase().includes(q); s.slice(0, 10); "a,b".split(","); arr.join(" · ");
key: Strings are IMMUTABLE — every method returns a NEW string.
ClosuresFunctions
Function + captured scope = private state and factories.
const createCounter = () => { let n = 0; return { up: () => ++n, value: () => n }; };
key: Data privacy without classes.
thisFunctions
Method call → object before dot; arrows inherit enclosing this.
user.hi(); // this = user ··· setTimeout(() => this.save(), 0); // inherits
key: Arrows for callbacks, methods for objects, never bare this.
querySelectorDOM
First / all matches via CSS selectors; closest() climbs up.
document.querySelector("#app .btn"); el.closest(".card"); list.querySelectorAll("li");
key: Scope searches (card.querySelector) and climb with closest().
DOM editDOM
textContent (safe) vs innerHTML (trusted only); create/append/remove; dataset; classList.
li.textContent = name; box.classList.toggle("open"); el.dataset.id;
key: User data → textContent/createElement. Always.
Events + delegationDOM
addEventListener; one parent listener + closest() handles infinite children.
list.addEventListener("click", e => { const b = e.target.closest("button"); if (!b) return; });
key: target = clicked; currentTarget = listener's element.
fetch + asyncAsync
await fetch → check res.ok → parse. try/catch/finally + timeout.
const res = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000) });
if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
const data = await res.json();
key: fetch resolves on 404/500 — check .ok yourself!
localStorageStorage
String-only forever-store. JSON + try/catch wrapper.
localStorage.setItem("k", JSON.stringify(v)); JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("k")) ?? fb;
key: Preferences only — NEVER tokens/secrets (XSS-readable).
JSONData
stringify (send/store) / parse (receive/load, wrap in try/catch).
JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2); JSON.parse(text);
key: Double quotes, no trailing commas, no functions.
ModulesOrganize

export const add = (a, b) => a + b; import { add } from "./m.js";
key: type="module" scripts are deferred + strict automatically.

Key takeaway — Key takeaway

Commit MESSAGES describe the change like a newspaper headline: "Add dark-mode toggle", "Fix mobile nav overlap". Future-you (and employers reading your GitHub) judge your professionalism by these lines. Never "fix", "update", "final-final-2".

Branching workflow (never break main)

git switch -c feature/quiz-timer     # new universe for the feature

Warning — Pushing .env = leaking keys to the world

Bots scan GitHub for keys within MINUTES. If you ever push a secret: revoke it immediately (new key), then clean history. Prevention (.gitignore from day one) beats surgery.

Angela §NodeElzero NodeMDN server

Node vs browser: same language, new powers

Table 89 — Browser JS vs Node.js
BrowserNode.js
Globalswindow, document, fetch, localStorageprocess, Buffer, __dirname-less ESM
SuperpowersDOM + UI eventsFiles, OS, network servers, thousands of connections
Missing(everything present for UI)NO document/window/localStorage!
Modules<script type="module">ESM in .js + "type": "module"
CODE  ·  Your first server (save server.js, run: node server.js)
import http from "node:http";
const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
  res.writeHead(200, { "Content-Type": "application/json" });
  res.end(JSON.stringify({ status: "alive", time: new Date().toISOString() }));
});
server.listen(5000, () => console.log("Listening on http://localhost:5000"));
Think of it like this — Node is a master waiter

One waiter (thread) takes ALL orders instantly and never stands at the kitchen waiting: chefs (libuv thread-pool) cook async and call back when ready. Blocking the waiter (slow sync loops, sync crypto) freezes the WHOLE restaurant — hence: never block the event loop.

Event loop + non-blocking (the rule behind everything)

CODE  ·  Blocking (evil) vs non-blocking (Node way)
import fs from "node:fs";
// EVIL in servers: freezes ALL users while reading!
const data = fs.readFileSync("big.json", "utf8");
// NODE WAY: everyone else keeps being served meanwhile ✔
const text = await fs.promises.readFile("big.json", "utf8");
Table 90 — Node async toolkit
ToolUse
fs.promisesFiles without blocking (read/write/append)
path.join/resolvePaths that work on Windows AND Linux
crypto.randomUUID()IDs, tokens (never Math.random for security!)
process.env.PORTConfig/secrets from environment (never hardcoded!)
CODE  ·  Everyday Node utilities
import fs from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import crypto from "node:crypto";
const file = path.join(process.cwd(), "data", "notes.json");
const notes = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(file, "utf8").catch(() => "[]"));
notes.push({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), text: "Hello", at: Date.now() });
await fs.writeFile(file, JSON.stringify(notes, null, 2));
const PORT = Number(process.env.PORT || 5000);   // env with fallback ✔
Quick check — fs.readFileSync in a request handler…
  1. Fine, it's fast
  2. Blocks ALL users until done — use fs.promises
  3. Only blocks one user
  4. Required for JSON
Answer: B  ·  Sync I/O on the event loop freezes every concurrent request. Sync is for startup scripts, never request paths.

REST design (nouns, verbs, codes)

Key takeaway — Key takeaway

URLs are NOUNS (/notes, never /getNotes); methods are VERBS; status codes narrate the outcome. Version from day one (/api/v1/…) — v2 will thank you. Error bodies share ONE shape: {error: {code, message}}.

Express setup + routing

CODE  ·  Minimal professional API (npm i express cors)
import express from "express";
import cors from "cors";
const app = express();
app.use(cors({ origin: "https://myapp.example" }));  // front-end origin ONLY
app.use(express.json({ limit: "100kb" }));           // parse JSON bodies (capped!)

let notes = [{ id: "1", text: "Learn REST", done: false }];

app.get("/api/v1/notes", (req, res) => res.json({ data: notes }));
app.get("/api/v1/notes/:id", (req, res, next) => {
  const n = notes.find(x => x.id === req.params.id);
  if (!n) return next({ status: 404, message: "Note not found" });
  res.json({ data: n });
});
app.post("/api/v1/notes", (req, res, next) => {
  const text = req.body?.text?.trim();
  if (!text) return next({ status: 400, message: "text is required" });
  const note = { id: crypto.randomUUID(), text, done: false };
  notes.unshift(note);
  res.status(201).json({ data: note });
});

Middleware: the assembly line

request → cors → express.json → logger → auth? → ROUTE → response Any step may: pass (next()), answer early (res.json), or fail (next(err)). ORDER MATTERS: app.use(auth) AFTER public routes protects only later ones!
Figure 18 — Request flows through middleware in order
CODE  ·  Custom middleware (logger + auth guard + 404 + error handler)
// Logger (first, sees everything)
app.use((req, res, next) => {
  console.log(new Date().toISOString(), req.method, req.url);
  next();
});
// Auth guard (use per-route: app.post("/x", requireAuth, handler))
function requireAuth(req, res, next) {
  if (req.headers.authorization !== `Bearer ${process.env.API_TOKEN}`)
    return next({ status: 401, message: "Unauthorized" });
  next();
}
// 404 for unknown API paths (AFTER all routes!)
app.use("/api", (req, res) => res.status(404).json({ error: { message: "Unknown endpoint" } }));
// Central error handler (4 args = Express knows; LAST!)
app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
  console.error(err);
  res.status(err.status || 500).json({ error: { message: err.status ? err.message : "Server error" } });
});
const PORT = Number(process.env.PORT || 5000);
app.listen(PORT, () => console.log(`API on :${PORT}`));
Warning — Middleware order bugs

express.json() AFTER routes = req.body undefined everywhere. Error handler NOT last = crashes bypass it. CORS misconfigured = browser blocks your own front-end. When Express "ignores" things, read your app.use order top-to-bottom.

Interview question — How do you structure an Express API?

Expected: "Thin routes, fat services: routes validate + call services; services hold logic; a data layer talks to the DB. Central error middleware with one error shape, request validation on every input, auth middleware on protected routes, and versioned paths." Bonus: rate limiting + helmet (Ch 45).

Quick check — Central error middleware signature?
  1. (req,res)
  2. (err,req,res,next)
  3. (res,err)
  4. (next)
Answer: B  ·  Four arguments mark it as error-handling; Express routes next(err) here. Placement: after all routes.

Validation, Files and Production Habits

Advanced~ 100 min

Validate everything (the validator pattern)

CODE  ·  Small validators, composed (no library needed to learn)
const isStr = (v, min = 1, max = 500) => typeof v === "string" && v.trim().length >= min && v.trim().length <= max;
const isId = v => typeof v === "string" && v.length >= 8;
function validateNote(body) {
  const errors = {};
  if (!isStr(body?.text, 1, 500)) errors.text = "text required (1–500 chars)";
  if (body.done !== undefined && typeof body.done !== "boolean") errors.done = "done must be boolean";
  return errors;
}
app.post("/api/v1/notes", (req, res) => {
  const errors = validateNote(req.body);
  if (Object.keys(errors).length) return res.status(400).json({ error: { message: "Invalid data", errors } });
  /* …create… */
});
Key takeaway — Key takeaway

Validate SHAPE (types/lengths/ranges) on every input — params, query, body. Return ALL errors at once ({errors}), not one-by-one (users hate fix-one-discover-next). Sanitize for storage, escape for display (XSS defense, Ch 45).

Pagination (never return 100,000 rows)

CODE  ·  Offset pagination with sane caps
app.get("/api/v1/notes", (req, res) => {
  const page = Math.max(1, Number(req.query.page) || 1);
  const limit = Math.min(100, Math.max(1, Number(req.query.limit) || 20));
  const q = (req.query.q || "").toLowerCase();
  const filtered = notes.filter(n => n.text.toLowerCase().includes(q));
  const start = (page - 1) * limit;
  res.json({ data: filtered.slice(start, start + limit),
    meta: { page, limit, total: filtered.length, pages: Math.ceil(filtered.length / limit) } });
});

Uploads without disasters

Table 92 — File upload safety rules
RuleWhy
Cap size (limits.fileSize)100MB "avatars" kill servers
Allowlist mime + extensionimage/* only — never trust client headers alone
Rename files (uuid)../../../etc/passwd names = path traversal attacks
Store OUTSIDE web root / use object storageUploaded .html/.svg can run XSS
Scan/resize images server-sideStrips malicious metadata, saves bandwidth
CODE  ·  Safe upload sketch (npm i multer)
import multer from "multer";
const upload = multer({ dest: "uploads/",
  limits: { fileSize: 2 * 1024 * 1024 },               // 2MB cap
  fileFilter: (req, f, cb) => cb(null, f.mimetype.startsWith("image/")) });
app.post("/api/v1/avatar", upload.single("avatar"), (req, res) => {
  res.status(201).json({ data: { file: req.file.filename } });
});

Production habits checklist

Ship-ready server review
  • - helmet headers + cors locked to your domains + rate limit on auth routes
  • - JSON body cap; ALL inputs validated; central error shape; no stack traces to clients
  • - Secrets ONLY in env/host dashboard; .env gitignored; logs without passwords
  • - Health route (/health); graceful PORT from env; process manager (PM2/systemd) + restarts
  • - Backups for file/DB data; dependency audits (npm audit) before releases
